name: stoat

attributes.attribute: a small red-brown Irish land mammal
viewed like a person, living in families
its spit was said to poison a full-grown man
unlucky to meet, but a greeting brings good luck

sources: Ó hÓgain, Dáithí. Irish Superstitions. London: Gill & Macmillan, 1995.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The stoat is a mythic animal of Ireland. It is a small red-brown land mammal that looks rather like a weasel. The folk of Ireland saw it as a person with a will. They said it lived in families and kept rites for its dead. The same animal was known for danger. Its spit was thought to poison a full-grown man. It was sly and given to thieving. It was unlucky to meet a stoat when you set out, even on a short trip. The way to turn the luck was to speak to the stoat as a neighbor. The stoat of Irish tales keeps both its great power and its small ways. It is a being of the road and of the house.
